tasks.spec:
You are authoring a MASTER SKILL. Your current working directory is a disposable task directory. Everything you produce goes here; you are NOT editing any repository and must not try to.

PRODUCE exactly two files:
  ./human-in-loop-oe/SKILL.md
  ./human-in-loop-oe/references/codex-macmini-setup.md
Also write ./notes.md at the task directory root.

WHAT THIS SKILL IS FOR. Its owner is Ankit. Any AI agent, on any machine, that is about to take an action needing his approval must not ask in chat and must not act. It raises a decision packet. Somewhere else, a mailroom turns that packet into a Linear card and buzzes his phone with two Telegram buttons, Approve and Respond. The agent waits for a recorded decision. This skill is the contract that agents follow.

THE FOUR STEPS the skill must teach:
1. RAISE. Append ONE JSON line to the local outbox file. Fields: packet_id (stable unique id the caller generates and later polls on), kind (approval for a yes/no gate, escalation for a heads-up), eli5 (one plain-English line, becomes the card title and the phone headline), department, action_class (external_send, crm_write, publish, deploy, spend, or proposal; be honest, it is the audit trail), urgency (normal or urgent; urgent REQUIRES due), due (ISO 8601 deadline), context (an object holding the sanitized evidence needed to decide), source_surface.
2. WAIT. The mailroom does the card, the buzz and the re-escalation. The agent does nothing.
3. READ BACK. Poll decisions.jsonl for a row whose packet_id matches. decision is approve, skip, or fix. On approve, do exactly the action described in the packet, nothing adjacent. On fix, read notes, revise, and raise a NEW packet with a NEW packet_id; never reuse the old approval. On skip, do not act.
4. NEVER claim the owner approved anything without that row.

HARD RULES the skill must state plainly:
- A decision exists ONLY as a row in decisions.jsonl. Not a chat message, not an inference, not silence.
- Waiting NEVER becomes consent. There is no timeout that converts a non-answer into an approval. He may answer in ten minutes or ten days; both are normal, and the channel re-pings him on its own.
- The agent holds NO credential. No Linear token, no Telegram token, no ssh key. It writes a packet; another machine does the card and the buzz. If a step seems to need a secret, that is the signal something is wrong.
- Never put secrets, health information, raw patient or contact identifiers, or raw message bodies in a packet. Describe the shape of the data, never the data.
- One packet, one decision, one action. Never batch unrelated approvals.

CADENCE, so callers know what to expect: a normal packet re-pings the owner every 48 hours, backing off after the third ping toward a two-week maximum, and never stopping. An urgent packet re-pings at half the time remaining until due, with a two hour floor, then every two hours once past due.

PORTABILITY IS THE POINT, and the check enforces it. This skill propagates from one private repo to Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and Gemini surfaces. Its body must therefore contain NO platform-locked construct: no allowed-tools declarations, no mcp__ tool names, no vendor-only command syntax, no assumption about which tools exist. Plain shell and plain Python only. Put every path in ONE config block near the top so a platform can override paths without touching logic. Per-platform differences belong in the deployment harness, not in the skill body.

FORMAT: SKILL.md opens with YAML frontmatter delimited by --- containing at least name and description. The description must make the skill discoverable, saying when to use it and when not to.

EVERY shell command you write, in either file, MUST be on a SINGLE line inside its own fenced bash block. Chain with && or ;. Backslash line continuations are forbidden. The owner copy-pastes these directly and a multi-line block breaks his workflow. This is checked.

THE SETUP REFERENCE, references/codex-macmini-setup.md, is what the owner hands to Codex running on a Mac mini. It must cover: which actions must go through this channel (external sends, CRM/EHR/finance writes, publishes, deploys, merges, spend above a ceiling, destructive operations, governance-file changes, and anything the agent is unsure about); installing the skill on that machine; where the outbox and decisions files live; and a VERIFY section walking an end-to-end test. That verify section MUST include a deliberate-failure step: poll for a packet_id that was never raised and confirm the agent reports that there is no decision rather than assuming one. Say why: a check nobody has watched fail is not a check.

WRITE ./notes.md recording what you decided, which portability traps you avoided, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no network. Do not edit any repository. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service. Invent no credential, no real path outside the ones named here, and no fake example token.
tasks.verified: an independent oracle confirmed SKILL.md has valid frontmatter with name and description, teaches the raise/wait/poll/never-assume contract with the full packet field set, states that waiting is not consent and that the surface holds no credential, contains no platform-locked construct that would break propagation to Codex/Hermes/Gemini, embeds no credential, and keeps every shell command on one line; and that the Mac mini reference covers install plus an end-to-end verify including a deliberate-failure step.

tasks.spec:
You are fixing a broken propagation script. Your current working directory is a disposable task directory. Everything you produce goes here; you are NOT editing any repository and must not try to.

PRODUCE exactly two files:
  ./sync-skills-to-surfaces.sh   (the corrected script)
  ./notes.md                     (your record)

READ THIS FIRST, READ-ONLY, it is the broken original:
  /home/ankit114/repos/Ankit-open-skills/skill-library/scripts/sync-skills-to-surfaces.sh

THE BUG, established by execution on 2026-08-05, not by reading. The private skill repo groups skills by FAMILY: skill-library/skills/base/<skill>/SKILL.md and skill-library/skills/program/<skill>/SKILL.md. Agent surfaces scan FLAT: they only find ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md and ~/.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md. The script rsyncs the whole skills/ tree, so it installs to <surface>/base/<skill>/, one level deeper than any surface looks. Evidence that this has never actually worked: neither surface has a base/ directory, and open-engine-card-format, which the owner's global AGENTS.md cites as canonical, sits in the repo and is installed on no surface at all.

FIX 1, FLATTEN. Skills must land at <surface>/<skill>/, with the family level stripped. A skill at skills/base/alpha/ must arrive at <surface>/alpha/.

FIX 2, COLLIDE LOUDLY. Once the family level is stripped, two families defining the same skill name would silently overwrite each other. That must be a hard failure: exit nonzero, and name the colliding skill and the families involved, before writing anything. A silent overwrite of a skill is exactly the kind of quiet drift this repo exists to prevent.

FIX 3, MAKE IT TESTABLE, and this one is not optional. The script currently hardcodes its source and both destinations, so merely testing it writes into the operator's live skill surfaces. A verification run on 2026-08-05 did exactly that and had to be cleaned up by hand. The corrected script must read its source from the SKILLS_SRC environment variable and its destination from SKILLS_DST, falling back to the current hardcoded values when those are unset so normal operation is unchanged. When SKILLS_DST is set, that single directory is the only destination.

PRESERVE: the existing --check mode that performs a dry-run diff rather than writing, and the existing conservative copy semantics. Do not make the script delete anything on a surface; a sync that can delete a skill is a bigger hazard than one that misses an update.

BE DEFENSIVE: set -euo pipefail, quote every path expansion, and fail with a clear message if the source directory does not exist.

VERIFY IT YOURSELF before finishing. Build a throwaway fixture tree in your own task directory with two families and one skill each, run your script with SKILLS_SRC and SKILLS_DST pointed at it, and confirm the skills land flat. Then add a colliding name and confirm it exits nonzero and names the collision. Put the exact commands you ran and their real output in ./notes.md. NEVER run the script without SKILLS_DST set to a throwaway directory; without it you will write to the owner's live surfaces.

WRITE ./notes.md recording what you read, what you changed, the exact verification commands and their real output, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no network. Do not edit any repository. Do not write anywhere outside your task directory. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service.
tasks.verified: an independent oracle refused to execute the script until it honoured SKILLS_SRC and SKILLS_DST, then drove it against a two-family fixture and confirmed skills land flat at <surface>/<skill>/ with no family directory, and that a same-named skill in two families causes a loud nonzero failure naming the collision instead of a silent overwrite.
